question: What percentage of tests will be positive for COVID-19 in the United States for the week ending October 10, 2026, in CDC data?
resolution_criteria: Resolves to the percent of tests positive for COVID-19 in the United States for the week ending 2026-10-10 in CDC's Percent of Tests Positive for Viral Respiratory Pathogens (data.cdc.gov dataset seuz-s2cv), as posted on 2026-10-30.
research:
# US COVID-19 test positivity, week ending 2026-10-10 (CDC dataset seuz-s2cv): research brief

## 1. Resolution source
- The data come from the CDC dataset seuz-s2cv on data.cdc.gov ("Percent of Tests Positive for Viral Respiratory Pathogens"). The columns are week_end, pathogen and percent_test_positivity, and the series starts with the week ending 2022-10-01. [data.cdc.gov](https://data.cdc.gov/resource/seuz-s2cv.json?$limit=5)
- 2026-08-22: 5.7% COVID positivity. This is the latest week that would have been published by 2026-08-31, since CDC posts on Fridays. Caveat: I took all values from the current version of the dataset, so earlier weeks may have been revised since they first appeared. [data.cdc.gov](https://data.cdc.gov/resource/seuz-s2cv.json?pathogen=COVID-19&$order=week_end%20DESC&$limit=60)
- Recent weekly values in 2026:
  - Jul 4: 1.4
  - Jul 11: 1.7
  - Jul 18: 2.1
  - Jul 25: 2.5
  - Aug 1: 3.3
  - Aug 8: 3.9
  - Aug 15: 4.7
  - Aug 22: 5.7
  - Positivity rose for 8 weeks in a row, and the weekly rise got bigger in August (+0.8, then +1.0).
- Earlier in 2026, the winter peak was 5.4% (Jan 24) and the spring low was 0.8 to 0.9% (May to June). Both are well below the same points in 2024 and 2025. [data.cdc.gov](https://data.cdc.gov/resource/seuz-s2cv.json?pathogen=COVID-19&$order=week_end%20DESC&$limit=60)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet. The target week is 7 weeks after the last published week. As of late August the summer wave was still growing and had not clearly peaked.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-08-25: The Sick Times published a national COVID trends update. [The Sick Times](https://thesicktimes.org/2026/08/25/national-covid-19-trends-august-25/)
- 2026-08-23: CDC wastewater showed COVID detected in all 50 states, but CDC's wastewater baseline labeled the level "very low." Stanford's WastewaterSCAN rated it "high." [Tech Times](https://www.techtimes.com/articles/325248/20260823/covid-hits-all-50-states-cdcs-wastewater-baseline-makes-rising-wave-look-routine.htm)
- 2026-08-20: CNN reported COVID climbing before the usual respiratory season. CDC estimated infections were growing or likely growing in 47 states as of Aug 19. Variants mentioned: NB.1.8.1 ("Nimbus") and BA.3.2 ("Cicada", about 15% of cases). [CNN](https://www.cnn.com/2026/08/20/health/covid-summer-wave)
- August 2026: Positivity passed 3% for the first time since March and was near 5% in mid-August, compared with above 9% at the same point in 2025. The article also notes widening surveillance gaps. [Medical Daily](https://www.medicaldaily.com/covid-test-positivity-three-percent-surveillance-gaps-august-2026-477601)
- Other coverage: [NBC Bay Area](https://www.nbcbayarea.com/news/health/summer-covid-cases-rising-every-state-symptoms-2026/4129843/), [Today](https://www.today.com/health/coronavirus/summer-covid-surge-symptoms-guidelines-2026-covid-vaccine-test-rcna592549).

## 4. Base rates and seasonality
Each year's change from late August to the week closest to Oct 10, taken from the same dataset ([data.cdc.gov](https://data.cdc.gov/resource/seuz-s2cv.json?pathogen=COVID-19&$order=week_end%20ASC&$limit=160)):

| Year | Late August | Peak | Early October | Change from late August |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2022 | before series start | n/a | 6.9% (Oct 8) | n/a; flat near 7% through October |
| 2023 | 14.6% (Aug 26) | 14.6% (Aug 26) | 10.0% (Oct 7), 9.2% (Oct 14) | about -32% |
| 2024 | 16.7% (Aug 24) | 17.9% (Aug 10) | 7.4% (Oct 5), 6.3% (Oct 12) | about -62% |
| 2025 | 12.0% (Aug 23) | 12.0% (Aug 23) | 5.4% (Oct 4), 4.2% (Oct 11) | about -65% |

- In 2023 to 2025 the summer wave peaked between mid-August and early September, then fell by 1 to 2 points a week through September.
- 2026 compared with past years:
  - The level is much lower (5.7% vs 12 to 17% in late August).
  - The wave is later: it was still climbing on Aug 22, while earlier years had peaked or were peaking by then.
  - The 2026 baseline is also lower overall: the spring low was about 0.9% vs about 2.8 to 3.1% in 2024 and 2025. That may reflect changes in testing or in the mix of labs reporting.
- Typical swing: over 7 weeks around this time of year, past values moved 4.6 to 10 points, which was roughly 30 to 65% of the late-August level.
- Week to week: values usually change by 0.3 to 1.9 points a week, and October values are sometimes revised slightly.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold market on this series.
- I found no published CDC or expert forecast of national test positivity. CDC publishes estimates of whether infections are growing in each state (Rt), not forecasts of positivity.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Weekly CDC updates come out on Fridays. The week ending Oct 10 should first appear around Oct 16, and the version that counts is the one posted on 2026-10-30, which may include revisions.
- When the summer wave peaks matters most. Past peaks fell in mid-August to early September.
- The spread of the BA.3.2 and NB.1.8.1 variants could keep positivity higher or make it last longer.
- School reopening in late August and September usually adds to respiratory transmission.
- The rollout of 2026-27 COVID vaccines in September and October could matter, as could reported surveillance gaps (changes in which labs report).
- The weather outlook is not directly relevant to this question.

Sources: [data.cdc.gov dataset](https://data.cdc.gov/resource/seuz-s2cv.json?pathogen=COVID-19&$order=week_end%20ASC&$limit=160), [CNN](https://www.cnn.com/2026/08/20/health/covid-summer-wave), [Medical Daily](https://www.medicaldaily.com/covid-test-positivity-three-percent-surveillance-gaps-august-2026-477601), [Tech Times](https://www.techtimes.com/articles/325248/20260823/covid-hits-all-50-states-cdcs-wastewater-baseline-makes-rising-wave-look-routine.htm), [The Sick Times](https://thesicktimes.org/2026/08/25/national-covid-19-trends-august-25/), [NBC Bay Area](https://www.nbcbayarea.com/news/health/summer-covid-cases-rising-every-state-symptoms-2026/4129843/), [Today](https://www.today.com/health/coronavirus/summer-covid-surge-symptoms-guidelines-2026-covid-vaccine-test-rcna592549), [GMA](https://goodmorningamerica.com/news/story/covid-cases-increasing-us-amid-summer-bump-111770385), [CIDRAP](https://www.cidrap.umn.edu/covid-19/covid-activity-continues-brisk-pace-across-much-us)
